chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
'The most beloved of my brethren to me is the one who presents my faults to me.'

key_terms.أَهْدَى إِلَيَّ عُيُوبِي: Presents/gives my faults to me — using the gift-giving metaphor (هدية) to frame honest criticism as a generous, valuable act
key_terms.إِخْوَانِي: My brethren — referring to spiritual brotherhood (ukhuwwa) among believers
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: A technical hadith term meaning the transmitter raised the chain to the Imam without naming all intermediate narrators (mursal/marfu')

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the most beloved companion or brother?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declared that the most beloved companion is not one who flatters, but one who sincerely shows a person their own faults — framing honest criticism as a precious gift. In the context of early Islamic community-building, this teaching countered the culture of sycophancy and emphasized that true brotherhood demands honesty even when uncomfortable. The Imam's use of 'أَهْدَى' (to give as a gift) elevates moral correction to the status of a generous act of friendship.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The most beloved of my brethren to me is the one who points out to me my faults’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad in a marfu’ manner from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
To me, the most beloved of my brethren (friends) is the one who most points out my defects to me.”
